long_biography.plain_text:
Levi discovered computer programming while studying business management and working part-time for a telephone company. After establishing himself as an independent consultant, he joined Roger Ray and Bob Shoup to create LRS in Springfield in 1979. The firm began with three employees in a small rented office and developed software for managing output from large IBM mainframes.

LRS expanded through organic growth and acquisitions, adding software, consulting, infrastructure, training and other technology services across several continents. Levi’s strategy emphasized debt avoidance and steady compounding while the company broadened its reach. He spent decades as president and chief executive, remains involved in major decisions, and now serves as chairman of the board.
